newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Ka-52 combat helicopter makes first flight.
newsitem.headline: Russian Ka-52 combat helicopter makes first flight.

text.p: A new Russian-made military helicopter, known officially as Ka-52 and informally as the Alligator, made its first flight on Tuesday at the Kamov design bureau's Lyubertsy aerodrome near Moscow.

The helicopter flew for six minutes making different manoeuvres at an altitude of 10 meters (33 feet). "It was a good flight...today we made the first flight and we are pleased with the results," test pilot Alexander Smirnov said after landing.
He said the helicopter needed more test flights, but that the pilots' first impressions were good.
Kamov president and chief designer Sergei Mikheyev told reporters that the two-seat Alligator was based on the single-seat Ka-50 combat helicopter, known as Black Shark.

"Alligator it is not a copy of Black Shark because Ka-52 is equipped with an upgraded radio-electronic system which allows it to observe several air and ground targets and to coordinate other helicopters above the field of combat," Mikheyev said.
Last November he said that the Ka-52 might cost $12 million to $14 million for foreign customers depending on what arms and equipment they want on board.
The Ka-52 will be displayed at the Moscow air show in August as well as a K-50 helicopter upgraded for combat at night.
Kamov has spent 18 years designing and building a single Ka-52 prototype and it plans to produce them at Arsenyev in the Russian Far East soon.
He gave no details of the armaments but said the new craft had French-made observation equipment. "Eighty percent of its components come from the Ka-50," he added.

Kamov hopes to get defence ministry orders for Ka-52s, which can be used as a training-combat aircraft or as a naval deck helicopter, but Mikheyev said the ministry had not financed their development.
"We are doing everything to find customers outside Russia," he said, without elaborating.
Mikheyev said the Arsenyev plant was ready to produce Alligators despite the fact that staff had not received their pay for 13 months.
"It is the record Russian salary delay," he said, adding that the Kamov designers and workers had not been paid for the past four months.
"The average (monthly) salary at Kamov is 877,000 roubles ($152)," he said, adding that a third of the staff had already resigned in recent years because of the low pay.
